name: orthotropic-cylinder-axisymmetric
reference: Benchmark C10. A cylindrically orthotropic thick tube under internal pressure, a = 0.1 m, b = 0.2 m, p = 60 MPa, axisymmetric with eps_z = 0. Under axisymmetry the engine's Voigt rows are already (rr, zz, theta-theta, rz), so material axes 1, 2, 3 are r, z and theta and cylindrical orthotropy needs no orientation at all: E_r = 10 GPa, E_z = 15 GPa, E_theta = 60 GPa, G_rz = G_r-theta = 5 GPa, G_z-theta = 6 GPa, nu_rz = nu_r-theta = nu_z-theta = 0.06. Lekhnitskii's solution (Anisotropic Plates, the cylindrically orthotropic tube): radial equilibrium with eps_z = 0 gives the Euler equation C_rr u'' + C_rr u'/r - C_tt u/r^2 = 0, so u = A r^k + B r^-k with k = sqrt(C_tt/C_rr), where C is the inverse of the 3x3 normal compliance. Here C_rr = 1.030954e10 Pa, C_r-theta = 3.991598e9 Pa, C_tt = 6.242207e10 Pa and k = 2.4606480774; A and B follow from sigma_r(a) = -p and sigma_r(b) = 0. That gives u_r(a) = 2.9723524491e-4 m, sigma_theta(a) = 157.716261 MPa, sigma_theta(0.15) = 46.6407238 MPa and sigma_theta(b) = 27.7361621 MPa. The stiff hoop direction pulls the load towards the bore: an isotropic tube of the same geometry carries sigma_theta(a) = 100 MPa (benchmark C2), so this row would fail by 58 % against the isotropic answer and is a real test of the orthotropic path rather than a restatement of Lame. The mesh is the (r, z) strip as 16 by 4 quad8 with u_z = 0 on both z edges, matching lame-axisymmetric's arrangement. Measured at 16 by 4: sigma_theta(a) = 157.1333 MPa (0.37 %), sigma_theta(0.15) = 46.5654 MPa (0.16 %), sigma_rr(a) = -59.7176 MPa (0.47 %), u_r(a) = 2.9723476e-4 m (0.00016 %). Doubling both divisions to 32 by 8 gives 157.5594 MPa, 46.6220 MPa, -59.9253 MPa and 2.9723521e-4 m, so each stress error falls by about four: the row converges to the closed form at the quadratic element's rate rather than passing at one mesh size.
